units.translation: about which in the Lexicon Sophocleum p. 131 I wrote this: "ἐάν [if] differs from εἰ [if] in that εἰ is a logical particle and one that refers simply to thought, whereas ἐάν is used for the signification of experience, as Hermann observed. That it is formed from εἰ ἄν [if + ever] is the opinion of the grammarians: see the scholia on Dionysius Thrax, in Bekker's Anecdota p. 951, 16. Etym. M. p. 307, 24. Eustath. p. 825, 26. Its forms are three, ἐάν [if], ἤν [if], and ἄν [if], of which the first two are used indiscriminately by the tragic poets and other old Attic writers, while the third belongs to later Atticism and the common dialect, as stated in the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 4. Where crasis with καί [and] is to be made, κἄν [and if] is written, not κἤν, which would be Ionic, not Attic. As regards quantity, not only is the first syllable long, by which it differs from the potential particle ἄν [ever], which is short, but also in the disyllabic form ἐάν the second syllable is lengthened, which, long unknown, I demonstrated from examples of comic and other poets, partly obscured by scribes and partly by editors, in my Oxford note on Arist. Wasps 228 p. 466. In the remains of the tragedians it happens by chance that only one example is found by which the quantity of this little word can be shown, Sophocles OC 1407 μή τοί με πρὸς θεῶν σφώ γ᾽, ἐὰν αἱ τοῦδ᾽ ἀραὶ | πατρὸς τελῶνται [do not, by the gods, you two, if this father's curses are fulfilled], where the codex has σφῶῖν γ᾽ ἄν [you two, if], which Elmsley corrected, and by that emendation he showed that he knew the correct quantity, while Brunck, ignorant of it, had written σφῶν ἐάν γ᾽ αἱ [you, if]." Another example of this quantity is perhaps to be restored to Sophocles OR 1062, where the codex has the faulty οὐδ᾽ ἐὰν ἐκ τρίτης ἐγὼ μητρὸς φανῶ τρίδουλος [not even if I am shown to be a slave from a third mother], where I conjectured οὐδ᾽ ἐὰν ἐγὼ ἐκ τρίτης [not even if I from a third], but with equal right οὐδ᾽ ἐὰν τρίτης ἐγὼ [not even if a third I] can be written with Hermann. The situation is almost the same in the Aeschylean passage Pr. 772, where in M is read οὐ δῆτα, πλὴν ἐγώ γ᾽ ἂν ἐκ δεσμῶν λυθείς [no indeed, except I, if released from bonds] (correctly λυθῶ [I be released] in the apograph), which I corrected thus: πλὴν ἐὰν ἐγὼ ἐκ δεσμῶν λυθώ [except if I be released from bonds].
The Aeschylean examples of the particle, which is constructed with the subjunctive alone, are these:

where it is uncertain whether ἐὰν δύνωμαι [if I am able] is placed in parenthesis or is constructed with πειράσομαι [I will try] in an indirect question, as in Plato Laws 1 p. 638e πειρώμενος ἂν ἄρὰ ἄρ δύνωμαι [trying if perhaps I might be able].
Of the second form ἤν [if] there are only two examples,
Do not, by the gods, you two, if this father's curses are fulfilled
not even if I am shown to be a slave from a third mother
not even if I from a third
not even if a third I
no indeed, except I, if released from bonds
except if I be released from bonds
I will try, if I am able, to release you from these toils.
trying if perhaps I might be able
if someone in due season softens the heart.
